column3: The Hebrew describes the blood as shed without cause; BSB calls it “innocent blood.”
The Hebrew coordinates the attacking and killing and separately says David did not know; BSB places that lack of knowledge before the killings.
The Hebrew names Joab’s head and the head of his seed separately in the singular; BSB combines them as plural “heads.”
The Hebrew leaves the man killed unnamed; BSB supplies Joab.
The Hebrew repeats “the king” as appointer and uses “in his place”; BSB uses “he” and supplies Joab.
The Hebrew separately says the king sent and called; BSB condenses this as summoning.
The Hebrew calls Kidron a wadi and intensifies dying by repetition; BSB uses “Valley” and states dying once.
The Hebrew says “the word is good” and “many days”; BSB uses “The sentence is fair” and “a long time.”
The Hebrew describes the report actively with unnamed people; BSB uses passive reporting.
The Hebrew names Shimei twice and repeats going; BSB names him once and says he brought them back.
The Hebrew gives his answer as “the word is good; I have heard”; BSB has “The sentence is fair; I will comply.”
The Hebrew explicitly names Shimei and repeats knowing with his heart as the second subject; BSB leaves the addressee implicit and says “know in your heart.”
The Hebrew leaves the struck man unnamed; BSB supplies Shimei.
